name: OpenAI API key
why: Anyone with this key can spend your money and read your usage.
fix: Move to .env as OPENAI_API_KEY, read via process.env on the server only, and rotate the key.

name: Anthropic API key
why: Anyone with this key can use your Anthropic account and billing.
fix: Move to .env as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, use server-side only, and rotate the key.

name: AWS access key ID
why: Leaked AWS keys are scanned for by bots within minutes.
fix: Deactivate the key in AWS IAM now, create a new one, load it from environment variables.

name: Stripe live secret key
why: Gives full access to your Stripe payments.
fix: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard and keep it in .env on the server only.

name: Stripe test secret key
why: Test keys are lower risk but should still not be committed.

name: Google API key
why: Can be abused for billing if not restricted.
fix: Restrict the key by domain/API in Google Cloud Console, move to .env, rotate if public.

name: GitHub token
fix: Revoke the token at github.com/settings/tokens and create a new one stored in .env.

name: Slack token
why: Gives access to your Slack workspace.
fix: Revoke and regenerate the token, store in .env.

name: Private key block
why: A private key in the repo lets anyone impersonate your server or account.
fix: Remove the file from the repo, rotate the key pair, load the key from a secret manager or env.

name: JWT token (possible Supabase service key)
why: JWTs may be a Supabase service_role key, which bypasses all row-level security.
fix: If it is a service_role key, rotate it in Supabase and use it server-side only. The anon key is meant to be public.

name: Hardcoded secret assignment
why: Hardcoded secrets end up in git history and client bundles.
fix: Move the value to .env and read it from process.env.

name: Secret exposed in public frontend variable
why: Variables with these prefixes are shipped to the browser, so everyone can read them.
fix: Rename without the public prefix and call the API from a server route instead of the browser.
